headline: Deep models link omics layers, histology, and clinical endpoints across cancer data
label: Deep Learning Multiomics Integration
summary: Semi-supervised, self-supervised, and cross-modal objectives are being used to extract information from unlabeled and multimodal cohorts.
synthesis: The dominant thread is deep learning that either exploits unlabeled data through semi-supervised or self-supervised objectives or predicts one molecular or morphological layer from another. Cox-MT applies Mean Teacher learning to ANN-based Cox models, using unlabeled TCGA data to improve prognosis prediction, while Srnc and scAURA use self-supervised representations for cell-type identification and clustering of scRNA-seq data. Cross-modal prediction appears in DeepGxP, which infers protein and phosphoprotein abundance from transcriptomes, and in HistoPrism and Hist2Cell, which infer gene expression and cell-type abundance from histology. What appears new is HistoPrism's pathway-level benchmark testing whether predictions are biologically coherent, and scTREND's time-resolved, condition-dependent hazard model linking single-cell states to survival. Reported results rest on distinct cohorts and endpoints rather than shared benchmarks, so direct cross-item comparison remains limited.
